import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 130

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/130](https://www.erdosproblems.com/130)
-/

namespace Erdos130

open EuclideanGeometry SimpleGraph

/--
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be an infinite set which contains no three points on a
line and no four points on a circle. Consider the graph with vertices the points
in $A$, where two vertices are joined by an edge if and only if they are an
integer distance apart. How large can the chromatic number and clique number of
this graph be? In particular, can the chromatic number be infinite?

The chromatic number can be infinite: there is an infinite general-position set
whose integer-distance graph admits no finite proper colouring. How large the
*clique* number can be is not addressed here.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-130/Research/Basic.lean"]
theorem erdos_130 :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∃ A : Set ℝ², A.Infinite ∧ InGeneralPosition A ∧
        (IntegerDistancePlaneGraph A).chromaticNumber = ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos130

reformulations.difference: Infinite chromatic number is expressed as equality to ⊤ in ℕ∞, rather than explicitly asserting the absence of every finite proper coloring.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib defines G.Colorable n as Nonempty (G.Coloring (Fin n)) and proves G.chromaticNumber ≠ ⊤ ↔ ∃ n, G.Colorable n. Negating gives G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ↔ ∀ n, ¬ G.Colorable n. This equivalence, including its use inside the existential statement, was proved in scratch. The source's explicit question asks whether the chromatic number can be infinite, not which infinite cardinal it equals.

reformulations.difference: The imported general-position definition expresses “no four points on a circle” using all subsets T ⊆ A satisfying T.ncard = 4 and forbids Cospherical T.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Set.ncard_eq_four characterizes exactly sets of four pairwise distinct elements, so the value ncard = 0 for infinite sets does not cause a loophole. Quantification over these subsets is equivalent to quantification over distinct quadruples. Cospherical means equal distance from a common center; with two distinct points that radius is necessarily positive. In ℝ² this is precisely lying on a circle. The quadruple equivalence and the positive-radius equivalence were both proved in scratch Lean.

review.notes:
No mathematical defect found in the sole declaration. It faithfully formalizes the source's explicit infinite-chromatic-number subquestion; the separate clique-number question is deliberately left unformalized, as the docstring says.

The proof record was substantively verified. All nine cited external Research modules were compiled in /workspace/review, with two proof-only compatibility edits for Lean 4.31→4.33 and no changes to definitions or statements. /workspace/review/bridge.lean translates their coordinate-based definitions and derives the complete repository statement. Both the external theorem and the translated proof have only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as axioms. Boundary and equivalence tests are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

The live source returned Cloudflare 403 responses, so its present-day wording/status could not be inspected directly. The archived page and current community database label the broader problem open; that is not sufficient evidence of a status error for this narrower, formally proved declaration. The target file was not modified.
